source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: By battery protection, are you referring to a hard short circuit across the battery terminals? Overcharge is already handled by the AXP2101, which cuts off at 4.45V, and its overdischarge cutoff is configurable at about ~2.4V. As for NTC, yes, we should add it to J\_BAT.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Ideally, the battery JST would sit next to the board JST, with both vertical, as shown in AM\_1.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Given that fit issue, the battery connector can instead go on the back, opposite the usb-c.

value_updates.battery_connector_placement: on the back, opposite the USB-C connector

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: After looking into it, I think a 2.0mm JST-PH with 3 pins would be better, carrying GND, VCC, and NTC. Is that possible to implement?

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: An SMD implementation would be preferable for the PH connector.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: Sorry, I realized the battery connection goes directly to the battery. What is the correct battery pinout, and is this connection last, so I can update my documentation?

ambiguity.description: The correct battery-connector pinout and labeling are unresolved after a possible mislabeling was identified.

routing_warnings.description: The inability to fit the connectors within the 68 mm board constraint is a general power-board mechanical-layout issue; the resulting battery-specific placement change is captured separately at message 77.
The J_BAT short-edge constraint applies to the later single integrated board rather than the power-board battery interface.
The battery-connector accessibility concern concerns the later integrated board and its enclosure-facing USB-C placement.
